tests_required.name: tests/test_build_sim_wires_route.py::test_a_sim_bot_with_a_persisted_wire_actually_routes
tests_required.observes: Build a two-bot sim fleet from configs carrying `_src_bot_id` A and B, import the single wire {source_id: A, target_id: B, pct: 20.0}, drive one SCRUM sell, and assert `_route_scrum_proceeds_via_wires` returns > 0 and that B's `apply_wire_income` was called. This is the test that distinguishes 'wired' from 'reported wired'.
tests_required.red_on_baseline_because: On the unmodified baseline the sim bot's id is a fresh uuid4 (bot_container.py:881), so `get_outgoing_wires(self.bot_id)` returns {} and the routine returns 0.0 at scrumming_bot.py:1788-1789. The assertion `routed > 0` fails while an import-count assertion would pass — which is exactly the discrimination required.

tests_required.name: tests/test_build_sim_wires_loaded.py::test_active_wire_count_is_endpoint_resolved_not_import_count
tests_required.observes: Feed a wire set where one endpoint is absent from the sim fleet; assert the reported ACTIVE count is len(wires) - 1, not len(wires).
tests_required.red_on_baseline_because: `import_wires` (smart_wire.py:456-478) performs no existence check against `_bot_refs` and returns n for every well-formed row, so any implementation that reports its return value passes at the full count. There is no such counter today, so the test is red for absence.

tests_required.name: tests/test_build_sim_no_live_manager.py::test_sim_wire_manager_never_emits_on_the_live_bus
tests_required.observes: Subscribe a spy to `get_event_bus()` for `bot.log`; run a replay whose wires fire a `distribute_fold_profit`; assert the spy received zero events. Premise control in the same file: assert a deliberately bus-less `SmartWireManager()` DOES reach the spy, so a zero is a measurement and not a dead instrument.
tests_required.red_on_baseline_because: If step 2 copies nuclear_fleet_controller.py:551's bus-less construction, smart_wire.py:508 falls through to `get_event_bus()` and the spy fires. The premise control is essential: with no wires registered, smart_wire.py:500-501 returns before the bus resolve, so a naive version of this test is green for the wrong reason.

tests_required.name: tests/test_build_sim_no_live_manager.py::test_apply_wire_income_is_never_called_on_a_non_sim_bot
tests_required.observes: Patch `ScrummingBot.apply_wire_income` with a spy recording `id(self)`; run a replay; assert every recorded id is in `{id(b) for b in ctl._bots}`. Covers all three `_bot_refs` dereferences: smart_wire.py:529 (source), :580 (fold target), and the scrum-time reach at scrumming_bot.py:1835/:1840.
tests_required.red_on_baseline_because: Red for absence today (no sim manager exists at all), and it is the only gate that would catch a future implementation reaching `BotManager.smart_wire_manager`, whose `_bot_refs` hold the same live objects `BotManager._bots` holds (bot_container.py:2349 then :2370).

tests_required.name: tests/test_fleet_replay_anchors.py::test_anchor_index_is_a_union_position_when_the_union_has_a_gap
tests_required.observes: Two synthetic series whose union omits k interior 5-minute slots; a trade after the gap; assert the returned anchor set contains the trade's UNION index and that the max anchor does not exceed the union size.
tests_required.red_on_baseline_because: controller:1154 computes `(ts*1000 - base) // 300_000`, a gapless-ruler slot, so the anchor lands k candles past the union position. Note the existing anchor tests (tests/test_fleet_replay_controller.py) build base and n_candles inside one synthetic uniform grid, so union == grid and they pass identically whether or not the defect exists — they have no positive control for this defect class.
